kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Super Starter Kit

identity.canonical_name: UNO prototype shield with SYB-170 mini breadboard
identity.manufacturer: generic; no single named manufacturer confirmed. Sold under many OEM brands (HiLetgo and similar) with an essentially identical design; ELEGOO does not sell this piece as its own standalone SKU
identity.manufacturer_part_number: generic proto shield with SYB-170 mini breadboard (no standardized MPN found)
generic_equivalents: any "SYB-170 mini breadboard" prototype shield for Arduino Uno
identity.package: module (shield PCB that stacks on the Uno via pin headers, with a mini breadboard stuck to the top)

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A blank circuit board that plugs on top of the UNO and gives you a small breadboard and solder pads, so you can build a circuit without a tangle of loose wires.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Building semi-permanent or compact circuits: stick components onto the small breadboard on top for a solderless build, or solder parts directly onto the prototyping grid underneath for something sturdier.
function.how_it_works_briefly: The shield's header pins on the underside plug straight into the Uno's own headers, extending every Uno pin up to a matching row of holes on top of the shield right next to the mini breadboard, so wiring a part is a short hop instead of a long wire run.

pins.pin_1_identification: There is no dedicated pin 1. Orientation is fixed because the header spacing only stacks onto an Uno one way, keyed against the USB/power-jack end of the Uno like any other shield.

electrical.operating_voltage: same as whatever the Uno underneath supplies (5V logic at the shield's header)
electrical.typical_current: negligible; the shield's own onboard LED circuit draws a few mA when used
electrical.interface: none (passive pass-through board, no chip of its own)

key_specs.onboard_extras: 2 LEDs (red, green) each with a matching resistor, 1 reset button, 1 general-purpose push button, two 0.1uF capacitors, a surface-mount pad area for chips up to 14-pin SOIC, gold-plated header pads, 0.1in x 0.1in prototyping grid, and a pass-through ICSP header so another shield can stack on top

visual_identification.shape_and_size: A rectangular PCB the same footprint as the Uno (about 7cm x 5.5cm) with two rows of female header sockets on the underside that plug straight down onto the Uno's pins, and a small breadboard (about 4.8cm x 3.4cm) stuck on top with its own grid of tiny insertion holes.
visual_identification.color_and_markings: PCB color usually matches other boards in the kit (commonly blue or red); the mini breadboard on top is white plastic with a printed red stripe (positive rail) and blue stripe (negative rail) along its edges.
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: A grid of prototyping pads near the header edges, plus a small reset button and an unlabeled general-purpose push button near one corner.
easily_confused_with: A full-size solderless breadboard (much bigger, no header pins to plug into a board)
A bare Uno shield with no breadboard on top
A perfboard/stripboard (bare copper pads, no adhesive breadboard on top)

required_extra_parts: jumper wires or direct component leads to use the mini breadboard or solder pads
wiring_to_uno.arduino_library: none; it is a passive board

hazards: Misaligning the header pins when pressing the shield onto the Uno can bend a pin
Careless soldering on the prototyping grid can bridge adjacent pads and short a signal to power or ground
handling_notes: Line up the header sockets carefully before pressing down; press evenly, not on one corner
Unplug USB power before attaching or removing the shield
common_mistakes: Assuming the mini breadboard's power rails are automatically connected to the Uno's 5V/GND (they are not, until you jumper them yourself)
Forgetting the shield adds height, which can make some enclosures not fit

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: Nothing on the shield's breadboard works
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: The breadboard's power rails were never jumpered to the Uno's 5V/GND pins
symptoms_and_causes.check: Run a jumper wire from a 5V pin on the shield header to the breadboard's + rail, and GND to the - rail, then re-check

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: Uno stops responding after attaching the shield
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: A bent or misaligned header pin is shorting two signals together
symptoms_and_causes.check: Remove the shield and inspect the header pins for bending before reseating

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: With the shield seated and the Uno powered, measure continuity between any GND point on the shield's header and the Uno's own GND pin; you should read near 0 ohm, confirming a solid connection.

confidence.notes: ELEGOO does not appear to sell this exact prototype shield as a separate product outside the kit, so price and detailed specs come from a generic-brand equivalent (Robot Pi Shop / HiLetgo-style SYB-170 proto shield) that matches the kit's description (mini breadboard, 170 tie points), per the brief's rule for kit-specific generic parts. This is a passive pass-through board with no chip of its own, so its header pins are treated as mirroring the uno-r3 record rather than re-deriving a separate confirmed table.
